title: Time Feels Slippery
pin_title: ADHD Time Blindness: Why Minutes Disappear
description: Time blindness means hours can vanish without a clear sense of how long something took. It is not carelessness. Pair every task with an external clock or a gentle timer you can see. Checking the time becomes a habit instead of a surprise. A visible clock helps your brain stay oriented without constant mental effort. #ADHD #TimeBlindness #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Reward the Start
pin_title: ADHD Motivation: Reward the First Small Step
description: Waiting for the whole task to finish before any reward can leave an ADHD brain stuck. Give yourself a tiny treat or a stretch right after the first two minutes of work. The brain learns that starting brings something nice, which makes the next start easier. Small rewards build the habit of beginning. #ADHD #Motivation #ADHDTips #Rewards

title: Move Then Return
pin_title: ADHD Focus: Use a Short Movement Break
description: Sitting still for long stretches can make focus harder with ADHD. Stand up, stretch, or walk for two minutes, then come back. The movement resets attention without needing a long break. Returning after a short walk often feels fresher than pushing through stiffness. Movement is part of the work, not an interruption. #ADHD #Movement #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Restart Kindly
pin_title: ADHD Restart: Speak Gently After a Pause
description: A pause or a missed day does not erase previous effort. When you return, say one kind sentence to yourself about the next tiny step instead of listing what was missed. Kind language lowers the shame barrier and makes the restart smaller. You can begin again as many times as needed without a speech. #ADHD #SelfCompassion #ADHDTips #Restart

title: Write the Next Step
pin_title: ADHD Planning: Name Only the Next Action
description: Long plans can freeze an ADHD brain. Write only the single next physical action on a note: open the notebook, fill the glass, press start. When that step is done, write the one after it. Naming only what comes next keeps the list short and the barrier low. One clear step is easier to begin than a whole project. #ADHD #Planning #ADHDTips #ExecutiveFunction
